title: Clear the hair from under a sink's open pop-up stopper: feed the hooked wand in under its head and draw the hair out
instruction: Clear the hair from under the sink stopper, then leave the tool and the hair on the counter.
context: Hair caught below a bathroom sink's pop-up stopper is the usual reason a sink drains slowly. Hooked wands such as the Drain Weasel are sold to clear it without taking the drain apart; the maker says the wand "will slide past most drain pop-up stoppers". The hair is out of sight and out of reach: the open stopper's head covers the drain, so the thin wand has to go in under its edge, bend down the bore beside the stopper and come back out with the hair.
setup: Metres; x forward from the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left, heights above the robot's table top. Vanity (fixed): 31 x 22 in (787 x 559 mm) stone top, 30 mm thick, surface 243 mm up, front edge x 0.105, left end y 0.3735, right end y -0.4135; closed cabinet below, cut off at the table top; wall and 100 mm backsplash behind; single-hole faucet behind the basin, spout 110 mm above the top. Basin: Kohler Caxton K-2205 under-mount vitreous china (432 x 356 mm oval opening, long side along y; 162 mm water depth; 44 mm drain hole; no overflow), drain at (0.360, -0.020). Drain: Kohler K-7114 pop-up without overflow, chrome brass; 54 mm flange 4 mm proud, top 55 mm up; 32 mm bore (est.); 3/16 in pivot rod from the back, 50 mm below the flange top (est.), through the stopper's eye; tailpiece cut off at the table top. Stopper (fixed, open): domed head 42 mm across (est.), underside 20 mm above the flange (est.); 36 mm gasket; four dark guide fins 30 mm across, 2 mm thick, at 30 and 120 degrees from +x (est.; the rod through the stopper's eye sets its turn); 9 mm stem. Hair: 0.50 g of 150 mm human hair (from a human-hair weft), wet, wound three turns round the stem among and below the fins and over the rod, filling the bore 22 to 52 mm below the flange top. Tool (loose): FlexiSnake Drain Weasel PLUS, orange reusable handle 133 mm (est.: 45 mm sleeve 30 mm square, grip 26 mm across, cap 30 mm across) with a 12 in (305 mm) wand (current refills are 18 in: trim one to 305 mm at its handle end), 3 mm thick (a 4 mm rod in the simulation), last 32 mm a dark 6 mm hooked pad; 56 g in the simulation (est.: handle with the wand's straight part 40 g, hinged end 16 g). A real tool is lighter at the wand (305 mm wand about 2-7 g, handle about 40-58 g, from retail listings) and balances about 34-59 mm behind where the wand meets the handle (est.); check once per tool that this is at most 55 mm. Lot A: lying on the top's front strip along its front edge, wand pointing to the robot's right, the wand's end of the handle at (0.135, 0.3085), 65 mm in from the top's left end, axis 15 mm above the stone; the grip and cap reach 68 mm past the top's left end; a checked real tool's balance point is then at least 10 mm in from that end, so it rests. Lot B: the tool 10 mm further right (58 mm past). Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Score 0 if at any time the tool drops off the vanity (any part more than 20 mm below the countertop outside the vanity's outline). Otherwise, at the end, with both grippers 10 mm or more from the tool and the tool still for the last 1 s, where 'the hair' is at least 0.40 g of the 0.50 g clump at the place named (blotted and air-dried 1 h, then weighed on a 0.01 g scale), 'drawn out' means hooked on the pad and pulled out of the drain by the tool (in simulation, only by the declared snag and a pull against the hair's load, see fidelity), and 'at the countertop's height' means inside the vanity's outline, no lower than 10 mm under the stone's surface (on the stone, or on the pad where the wand's end reaches past the rim): 1.0 the hair drawn out and at the countertop's height and the whole tool lying on the countertop (both ends of the sleeve on the stone; yes, the handle alone may reach past the top's edge, by up to 75 mm, as it starts with 68 or 58 mm, resting there by itself; every other point inside the outline; every point between 10 mm below and 40 mm above the stone's surface, none hanging into the basin); 0.5 the hair drawn out and at the countertop's height but the tool not lying so; 0.25 the hair drawn out of the drain (outside the flange, or 10 mm or more above its top) but not at the countertop's height (in the basin, or dropped past the top's edge); else 0. Read from a top photo, a straightedge across the rim with a ruler, a ruler along the top's end, the scale, and the video for release and stillness. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz) per lot
reset_notes: 1. Under the basin undo the pivot nut, draw the rod out of the stopper's eye, lift the stopper out; clear any hair left (torch, tweezers), blot and air-dry it 1 h, weigh it. 2. Hair: 0.50 g (+-0.02 g) of 150 mm strands cut from one human-hair weft, soaked 1 min and drained 30 s; wind it three snug turns round the stem among and just below the fins, ends tucked under the last turn; check with a ruler that it spans 42-72 mm below the head's underside (22-52 mm below the flange when open). Spare stoppers can be wound ahead, so a reset is a stopper swap (about 5 min). Refit the stopper, push the rod back through its eye and the hanging hair, refit the nut; the fins at their flange marks. 3. Lift rod down: stopper fully open (head 20 mm above the flange). 4. Fit a new wand (18 in refill trimmed to 305 mm at its handle end). 5. Lay the tool at its lot's marks (wand to the right, its handle's wand end 65 mm (A) or 75 mm (B) in from the top's left end); check it rests untouched 10 s. 6. Arms at ready. Run with -E object_jitter=0. The real clump's pull-out force is not measured; the simulation uses an estimate.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; the wand (last 128 mm 8 spring-hinged links, stiffness est.) collides with head, fins, flange, rod. Hair is a declared rule, not colliding: the barbed pad snags it only by going 10 mm in and drawing back 8 mm; till it reaches the flange top a force on the pad opposes its rise, 3 N at 4 mm/s up (est.: few wet strands, 0.5-1 N each); jerked over 0.10 m/s, pushed back over 5 mm or crept out under 2 mm/s, it stays; free, it passes the head unresisted. No water, spin; stopper fixed.
scores: Dream-1 runs: 0.0 (lot A 0.0, lot B 0.0) on this source; 0.0 (0.0, 0.0) before a scoring-only fix; 0.0 (0.0, 0.0) on the first version; demo: 1.0 (lot A 1.0, lot B 1.0; hair snagged 8-9 mm into the draw, then about 3 s of load averaging 2.2-2.3 N while drawn out, no breakaway)
